cells.tense: You are moving with your feeling right now, and the two are not arguing.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep meaning to begin and give it twenty minutes today, before you decide whether it is the right one.
cells.core:
What you want and what you do are going the same direction, and you can feel it. You start things without arguing yourself into them first, so the effort lands light — nothing inside you is pulling the other way. That is rarer than it feels from in here.

There is still something open in front of you, one of those things you haven't settled, and this is the good way to be standing in it. You are not stuck for lack of direction. You are early, and everything is still available. Give the first real move the same ease you give the small ones, and notice that you got to pick while it was still wide.

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a version of this that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Choose one open thing and take a single small real step on it, letting the step stay smaller than the plan you've been carrying.
cells.core:
You are leaning into what is coming before it is here. Somewhere ahead is the version where this is settled and proven, and you are living there already — rehearsing, preparing, running it through — while the moment you are actually in has not been given a chance to show you what it wants. Preparing for it costs more than the thing itself will.

What you have instead is wide open and undecided, and that is not a problem to solve fast. The direction underneath is real and it is sound. It runs cleaner when it moves from what you feel today rather than from an account that ought to be closed by now. One honest step, at the size of now.

cells.tense: You stopped walking toward what was open and you are still standing at the doorway.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you've been holding off starting, and let their reply be the whole of what you do about it today.
cells.core:
There is something you could start and you are not starting it. Your hand is still on the door — half in, half out — instead of turning around, and what you feel about the thing is still there. It just stopped turning into motion somewhere along the way.

Nothing here needs forcing; pushing yourself harder is not the fix. What is missing is smaller: an ending you didn't let finish, so the next thing has nowhere to grow from. Let one thing actually be over. Then say out loud what you want next, to someone who will hear it, and let that be enough for today.

cells.tense: You are already steering this toward one option while telling it as though nothing were decided.
cells.ask: Tell one person the thing you have quietly settled on starting, and say it as your call and not as something you'll see about.
cells.core:
You lean one way whenever this subject comes up, and you can feel it — what you bring up first, what you drift back toward, which version gets your attention without being asked. Working well, that pull is the whole point: a direction you can build on, moving from what you genuinely want instead of from a shortlist you keep re-reading.

Right now it stays technically open, out loud, in front of people. What stays open stays unbuildable, and the thing you actually want doesn't get your weight behind it. More certainty is not the missing piece. Naming it out loud is the move: plain, to one person, in your own voice, as the pick it already is.
